subject.title: gateway install/status hardcodes ~/Library/LaunchAgents — prevents boot-without-login on macOS

question: What privileged macOS LaunchDaemon contract should OpenClaw support for gateway install/status and the related lifecycle surfaces?
rationale: The remaining work chooses a security boundary for root-owned launchd files, sudo/operator flow, execution user, service environment durability, and coexistence with user LaunchAgents; automation should not choose that policy alone.

options.title: Explicit audited system scope
options.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as default, add an explicit LaunchDaemon install/status/lifecycle contract with owner-reviewed sudo, UserName, TMPDIR, doctor, docs, and tests.

options.title: Diagnostic guidance only
options.body: Do not manage LaunchDaemons yet; make status/doctor/docs clearly detect and guide operators who own custom system daemons manually.

options.title: Defer to current custom setup
options.body: Leave LaunchDaemon support out of core for now and keep the issue open only as product backlog until maintainers sponsor the privileged surface.

recommendation.title: Explicit audited system scope
recommendation.body: Keep user LaunchAgent as default, add an explicit LaunchDaemon install/status/lifecycle contract with owner-reviewed sudo, UserName, TMPDIR, doctor, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for the gateway lifecycle and service adapter boundary and is the best available owner for the launchd scope decision.
